mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-on-month increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a flat or declining housing starts series (HOUST) suggests a shift from durable goods to services consumption, which historically correlates with lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to sector rotation.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.3% MoM and HOUST <= previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows >0.3% MoM and HOUST is flat or declining.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) below 50k persons month-on-month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals labor market cooling that precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS < 50k for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of extreme inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5% YoY).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST above 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST are above 12-month averages and CPIAUCSL <= 5% YoY.
